As you know, the notion of a federation is quite something else. It does not include the notion of an entity and the people at large found it very difficult to accept that. They took it emotionally, although we know that one should not rely on emotions, one has to accept matters rationally. My view of that settlement was that it was better than the settlements that were being passed around at the time. I did not see it as part of something that would become Croatia but the people are entitled to an opinion, to formulate that opinion, and to advocate their opinions. What remains, of course, to be defined is in what way they want to attain this objective of theirs. In my view of the matter was that it should be through talks with the international community.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Dr. Zoric, thank you for that and believe it or not, I am trying to assist you by hopefully moving forward to see if we can possibly complete your testimony today. My final topic, my final question, I suppose, depending on your answer, there might be one or two follow-up questions. I just want to direct your attention to the text immediately following, immediately below the question, "Do you mean Mate Boban?" And you say, well, the question is "Do you mean Mate Boban?" And your answer is, "I mean Tito's youth who rule BiH nowadays. Those who did their best during work-drives to earn shock-workers' badges. Some people who nowadays lead the HDZ as the people's party of the Croats in the BiH and therefore as my party too were in their time bringing in for an interview even the first founders of the HDZ. They are very skillful political executors but they are unskilled with their own people whom they chase from pillar to post, driving finally many of the people in Herzegovina crazy too." Can you please tell the Judges when you refer to Tito's youth and the people who nowadays lead the HDZ in BiH, who are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see, I didn't want to name any names, I wanted to encourage, through my answer, the people in that part of the world to seek new faces. As you know, in young democracies, it is best for the officials to fluctuate. I don't know how far my answer could be deemed to be politically correct, but the term of Tito's youth was not something that was deemed in a positive light at the time and I believe that this would incite them to engage in a process of looking for new people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, it's my job that I have to ask you the question whether despite the fact that it may make you uncomfortable, which I might personally regret that, but I am required to ask you what individuals did you have in mind? Please give us, if you can remember, give us the names of the individuals you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have anyone specifically in mind. As you can see for yourself, I spoke in very general terms. My intention was to give the people in the area food for thought and to tell them that they should carefully look for new people who would lead them. You see what the journalist's question was. His question referred to a specific person whereas I, in my answer, did not refer to any individuals. I know that subsequently, there was change in that quarter, some new people emerged replacing the ones who were there before and I believe that change is always beneficial.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sometimes. The question to you was, "Do you mean Mate Boban ?" And of course you could have answered the question very quickly, "Yes," but you didn't. You didn't. You said, "I mean Tito's youth who rule BiH nowadays." Then going down to the next line, "Some people who nowadays lead the HDZ ..." Now, sir, you must have known, I'm sorry, but when you said, "Some people who nowadays lead the HDZ," you knew exactly who you were talking about. So please tell us who those persons were.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would definitely not have voted for me, I see. That was the way I spoke in public. I was trying to be active in politics at the time and I told you that I wasn't very good at it and I went back to the job that I am good at. Perhaps I should have given a more straightforward answer here but I did not and I cannot speak in hypothetical terms about what I specifically had in mind 15 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, I must say I wasn't laughing at you, I was laughing with you because I know that these things can be difficult, we try to find some humour where we can. But, sir, I have to conclude with this and I will leave it up to the Judges if they want to press you further but I put it to you, sir, that you do in fact know who you were talking about and you just don't want to tell us. Isn't that true? Yes?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it will be highly improper of me to name names here 15 years later. I don't think it would be proper on my part and I believe that I achieved as much as I wanted to achieve. If you want me to, I can answer the question that you put to me that remained unanswered from before the break because there was a procedural dispute about it. If I recall well, you asked me -- if that was important for you, I can give you an answer. If not, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me conclude with this, I will leave you in the Chamber's hands. If the Chamber wants to press you further for that information then the Judges can choose to do so. I want to thank you despite some rather firm questions, I thank you for coming to The Hague and giving your testimony. I wish you a safe return and that concludes my questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have 12 minutes left for redirect. Do you have any additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I do and just picking up on that last question. If the gentleman wishes to go into private session and name names, if he remembers, that may make it more comfortable assuming that he has specific names because that option was not given to him by the Prosecution. So if we were to go into private session, sir, would that make it ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we can move into private session if you so wish.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know what a private session is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, private session, that is a situation in which nobody knows what you could say unless -- but for the people who are in this courtroom, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me respond this way: "De mortuis nihil nisi bene."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We may need a translation for that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It means that of the dead, nothing unless it's good. It means that one should not slander persons after they -- one should not say the truth perhaps after they are dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: With that I just have some very quick questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On page 2 of today's transcript, there was a question with respect to refugee status and at one point you said that there was some misuse of the refugee status and as a result, there was some changes so that that status was only allowed for three months and then that there would be some -- they would have to check in once a month to review their status and what have you. Very briefly, when you said "misuse" were you speaking of Croats and Muslims both, and if so, could you give us just very illustrative, just one example of what kind of misuse you are talking about? Keep it brief because I have 10 minutes, sir.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have members of an ethnicity specifically in mind. This was not a feature that was unique to one ethnic group only. We tried to prevent these as far as we could. This was not a prevailing practice. If it was, then we prevented it. This was something that could be found among the Croat and Muslim refugees alike who tried to misuse their status by obtaining benefits that did not belong to them in the first place. That is what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you were asked a question, you were asked a question by the Prosecution and it was somewhere in the -- on page 31 about returns and you said words to the effect that safety was one and of course you were pressed with another question and you admitted, yes, accommodation was another. This is today's transcript, it's not in the documents, sir. Sir, it's not in your documents, it's in the transcript. So with respect, you indicated today that trying to return folks back to where they came from, you had to look at safety and accommodation; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we could look at one particular example, for instance, in 1D 01593, I have a copy for the gentleman, if I could have the assistance of Madam Usher and I have copies for everyone else. It is in the e-court system and then you could distribute this to everyone else. One to the Prosecution and then the Bench as well. Now, here is an example, for instance, this is a letter dated 7 April 1994. If we flip to the second page, we see that it's signed by Dr. Jadranko Prlic, president of the government and it's addressed to the president of the government of the Republic of Croatia, Mr. Nikica Valentic. Was Mr. Valentic the president at that time of the government?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the prime minister at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now it appears from the letter, if we were to look at it, and in this letter Dr. Jadranko Prlic is indicating that for some reason, there was a lack of coordination and that folks were being returned and that he was concerned that perhaps the areas where they were being returned were not quite ready to receive them.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we came across such situations when regarded from Zagreb some areas seemed safe whereas the local authorities knew better. We were looking at the municipalities within their territorial boundaries as at 1990. However, in the meantime, the territorial organisation and structure changed. Secondly, the municipalities covered wide territories and some of the specific locations within the municipality could still have been unfit for return although other parts were fit for that process and the authorities back in Zagreb could not be fully familiar with the situation. I believe that this is a request on the part of Mr. Prlic to stay a decision passed by Mr. Adalbert Rebic whereby the population should return to the BH and he states therein that he has the support for this of the people from -- both from Sarajevo and Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Suffice it to say if we look at this letter, it would appear that, at least from Croatia's part, some errors might have been occurring. In other words, they're trying to -- they may think that areas are safe and there's a lack of coordination; am I correct in that?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both options were possible. If they were unsafe areas and Zagreb didn't know about it, then we're talking about`poor coordination and communication, but there had been such situations before and there were similar situations after and each such decision could be reviewed and corrections were made. If return to a place was impossible or impossible for some people, then they would stay where they were, the decision was revoked, et cetera. I think this is about such a case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you're not a lawyer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not and I'm glad I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, very well. Now, you were pressed on some questions with respect to refugees, citizenship and what have you and you gave some answers and having spoken about my client during the break, he had indicated to me that his family, his wife, for instance, who was from Herzegovina went to Croatia, got citizenship, but at the same time because of the conditions was also able to have refugee status which was important, if for no other reasons, for health care. Now, sir, was that a possibility, do you know? Do you know how the law was structured? And be very quickly about it because I have a couple more questions.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of such situations, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you were asked about Tudjman's policy to carve-up Bosnia and Herzegovina and in the Tuta-Stela case, for instance, you had indicated that it was widely noted in a statement by the high representative of the UN in Sarajevo General Klein, that would be Jacques Klein, that Izetbegovic had offered Herzegovina to Tudjman and Tudjman had declined it. Do you recall that part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that part and I remember the statements given by General Klein. Yes, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And also you indicated, to be fair, that in the press that then came out that Izetbegovic was not denying that but then he was putting a sort of a spin or qualification that "... this was a tactical move to embroil Croatia in another type of game where, in my mind at least, it would never, ever be able to liberate its own occupied territories, Vukovar and Knin, because of some other principles would have applied in that case ..." and I'm reading from the revised transcript, not the one that the Prosecution indicated, but these are pages 11.080 to 11.081. Now, do you stand by that, sir, that you recall Izetbegovic in the press putting his spin that this was just a tactical move in order to embroil Croatia to see maybe if Tudjman would have taken the bite and the bait, as it were, and then he could use that for tactical reasons?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shows that apart from the job of a lawyer, there is another very difficult and demanding job, namely politics and that's why I don't do either. I spoke several times with Mr. Izetbegovic in his office in Sarajevo. As far as circumstances allowed, we also discussed political issues. My conclusion was exactly what you quoted. But that's how it goes in politics. Everybody tries to attain their goals and used different means to do so. It is my impression that Mr. Izetbegovic would sign anything he was given to sign just to get another opportunity. He signed a lot of things, first with Boban and then immediately after that with Karadzic, he signed a confederation or federation with Croatia, but then that idea was given up. His goal was the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: One final question here about Tudjman, because I think we want to make sure we fully understand. You indicated that this was a unity government, different factions. Sir, within -- at that time, is it not a fact that Tudjman had a lot of different players with a lot of different agendas, some thinking that the borders should be at the Drina which would have encompassed all of Bosnia-Herzegovina; others, the Banovina. Others wanted all sorts of different variations and isn't it a fact, sir, that Tudjman was playing one side against the other in order to achieve his own goal which was an independent Croatia within its recognised borders? Can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is an adequate assessment of him. I don't believe that the groups that advocated a Greater Croatia reaching to the Drina River were significant or powerful but there were some people. There was some hot heads advocating that not necessarily in the people around Tudjman, but many people were moving around him. He used many people to attain his goal both internally and internationally and I believe that in a rather long period, he was able to achieve his goals. Some people had a much -- didn't -- weren't able to look into the future for -- as far as he did but President Tudjman was aware who was on the other side, who was against him and I believe that he was able eventually to attain his goal. It was difficult but he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I did want to make one comment about the next witness but I can do so even by way of e-mail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Witness, thank you. We are sort of pressed by time but I thank all the parties for making it possible for you to complete your testimony. I know you have other commitments which I understand perfectly well. The Trial Chamber wishes you a safe return to your other commitments. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just wanted to thank the witness, too, on behalf of everyone here because I didn't get a chance to thank him and I forgot actually but we do appreciate him coming here so we thank him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing stands adjourned. We have another witness next week in the same conditions as for this witness. I think it's going to be Dr. Rebic, four hours --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said four. So we shall reconvene next week in the afternoon, 2.15 on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of May, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.
